title: Supreme Court: Hall v. Hall
summary: When one of several cases consolidated under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 42(a) is finally decided, that decision confers upon the losing party the immediate right to appeal, regardless of whether any of the other consolidated cases remain pending. (No. 16-1150, opinion by Chief Justice Roberts; 584 U.S. 59).

title: Supreme Court: Ayestas v. Davis
summary: The District Court’s denial of petitioner’s request for funding for “reasonably necessary” services of experts, investigators, and the like, 18 U. S. C. §3599(f), to develop his claim that both his trial and state habeas counsel were ineffective was a judicial decision subject to appellate review under the standard jurisdictional provisions; the Fifth Circuit did not apply the correct legal standard in affirming the denial of that request. (No. 16-6795, opinion by Justice Alito; 584 U.S. 28).

title: Supreme Court: Marinello v. United States
summary: To convict a defendant under 26 U. S. C. §7212(a)—which forbids “corruptly or by force or threats of force . . . obstruct[ing] or imped[ing], or endeavor[ing] to obstruct or impede, the due administration of [the Internal Revenue Code]”—the Government must prove the defendant was aware of a pending tax-related proceeding, such as a particular investigation or audit, or could reasonably foresee that such a proceeding would commence. (No. 16-1144, opinion by Justice Breyer; 584 U.S. 1).
